models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Very light, benign pattern over the Aeolians - useful as a pattern read only, far too early for the trip dates.
briefing.synopsis: The current picture is a slack, low-gradient regime: winds across all six islands are running 1.5-6.7 kt through 2 Oct on the model consensus, with a repeating diurnal swing from E/NE overnight and morning into N/NW by evening, and seas essentially flat at 0.1-0.3 ft. ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 29 Sep 18Z) and ICON-2i (29 Sep 12Z) agree on that character, with only two hours flagged for real spread - Portorosa 01 Oct 00:00 (models range 0.4-7.1 kt) and Filicudi 01 Oct 12:00 (2.0-8.9 kt). The forecast horizon in this payload reaches 06 Oct 23:00, so the first two or three trip days are just coming into range and the back half of the itinerary is not covered at all. Treat everything below as pattern, not prediction.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Tonight is not a fleet night - the flotilla is still ashore and departure is three days out. For the planned first night, 03 Oct at Portorosa, the payload shows Portorosa Marina as the recommended berth, ESE 3.3 kt gusting 8.7 with 0.1 ft swell - an enclosed marina with all-round shelter, so the berth choice does not matter at these numbers. Only a genuine gradient wind event would change that, and nothing in this data shows one.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: For planning rather than tomorrow specifically: in this pattern the light easterly overnight/early hours are the steadiest part of the day, and the computed recommended departure for every forecast leg is 06:00. Expect motoring more than sailing if it holds - several windows fall below 3 kt. Re-brief on the 12Z and 18Z runs each evening as the trip dates come into range; the numbers below will move.

passage_notes.note: Computed go, recommended 06:00: SSE 5.5 kt, gusts 11.5, waves 0.1 ft, a run at TWA 177. Wind backs to E then NE and falls to 2-4 kt by midday.
Computed go, 06:00: ENE 2.9 kt, 0.1 ft. Close-hauled early, head-to-wind and motoring from mid-morning as it veers NE/NNE at 2-3 kt.
Computed go but a motoring passage - 2.2-4.5 kt ENE/NNE all day, TWA 8-23, 0.1 ft seas. Budget fuel and daylight for 26 nm.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: Computed go, NE/ENE 4.7-5.4 kt, gusts to 13.6 by mid-afternoon, 0.2-0.4 ft. A run or broad reach; at the far end of the horizon, so low confidence.

cautions: Trip dates 07 Oct onward (Panarea → Filicudi, Filicudi → Salina and beyond) are past the 06 Oct 23:00 horizon - I have no forecast for them. The rehearsal runs in the payload are a dry run against this week's weather, not a forecast for your dates.

Stromboli's Marina del Gabbiano is scored only 'workable' (0.918) - open from every direction, no anchoring permitted, and shelter there depends entirely on it staying calm. Do not commit to the optional Stromboli night without a fresh forecast.
Gust figures against 2-5 kt means (10-14 kt in several windows) are interval-maximum values from a single model in light air, not sustained squalls - reported, not a threat.
Wind direction is the least reliable element in this pattern: forecast stability shows mean direction shifts of 47 degrees at 48-72 h and 65 degrees at 72-120 h, so plan points of sail loosely.
briefing.confidence_note: Models agree closely on the light-wind, flat-sea character - mean wind shift between runs is only 0.6-0.8 kt at 48-120 h - but direction drifts 47-65 degrees at those leads and most of the itinerary sits beyond the 06 Oct horizon.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
